note: Brand marks Mode draws to identify external apps and services (10 §7.4.16, ADR-0053). `source` names the public set the file was fetched from: simple-icons (CC0 1.0, monochrome paths), lobe-icons (MIT, monochrome AI marks), logos (gilbarbara/logos, the owners' full-colour marks), vscode-icons (MIT, full-colour product tiles); commons (Wikimedia Commons, with the licence the file page states in each mark's `licence`); fluent (Microsoft's Fluent UI brand-icons CDN, under the Fluent UI assets licence); `drawn` is kept only for the plain terminal window and the Kitty cat, which no set carries. `color` is `own` (the file carries its colours; the stylesheet sets none, so the mark stays right on a dark ground), the brand's hex for a monochrome mark, or `fg` for a near-black monochrome mark that follows the text colour. `ui/scripts/fetch-brand.mjs` fetches and normalises a mark; `ui/scripts/brands.mjs` generates the kit, the stylesheet block and the wireframe symbols from this file.

grounds.note: The reference surfaces a brand colour must read on at 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11): the darkest ground of a built-in light pack (Gruvbox Light's sunken fill) and the lightest ground of a built-in dark pack (Nord's surface). ui/scripts/brands.mjs moves a colour's lightness in OKLab until it reads; the hex stays where it already does.
